reviewStatus: Drafted from verified sources; pending independent clinician review before clinical release.
commonErrors: Measuring the haematoma rather than the nidus.
Treating any grade as a decision to operate or not.
Counting a deep-draining vein only when it is the sole drainage (any deep drainage scores 1).
name: Spetzler-Martin AVM Grade

version.label: Spetzler-Martin grading system (1986), grades I–V
version.detail: Size (<3 cm 1, 3–6 cm 2, >6 cm 3) + eloquence of adjacent brain (0/1) + venous drainage (superficial only 0, any deep 1). Grade VI (inoperable lesions) is described separately and is not calculated. The Spetzler-Ponce three-tier classes are a different system.

purpose: Grades brain arteriovenous malformations by features associated with surgical risk.
intendedPopulation: Patients with brain AVMs being assessed for treatment, using angiography and MRI.

calculatorNotice.title: A grade, not a treatment decision
calculatorNotice.message: Treatment depends on presentation, age, AVM features beyond the grade, natural history and patient preference, in multidisciplinary discussion.

options.label: Eloquent
options.detail: Sensorimotor, language or visual cortex; hypothalamus or thalamus; internal capsule; brainstem; cerebellar peduncles; deep cerebellar nuclei.

options.label: Any deep drainage
options.detail: Any drainage into deep veins (e.g. internal cerebral veins, basal veins, precentral cerebellar vein).

resultStates.label: Grade {roman(total)}
resultStates.detail: Lower grades were associated with lower surgical morbidity in the original series.

resultStates.label: Grade III
resultStates.summary: Spetzler-Martin grade III: a heterogeneous group.
resultStates.detail: Grade III includes AVMs with very different combinations of features; review the components.

resultStates.label: Grade {roman(total)}
resultStates.detail: Higher grades were associated with higher surgical morbidity in the original series. Management depends on presentation, AVM features and patient preference.

clinicalContext.text: Predicts the risk of surgical resection from size, eloquence and venous drainage.
Often combined with the Lawton-Young supplementary grade, which adds age, rupture and nidus diffuseness.

clinicalInsights.text: Grade III is heterogeneous (e.g. small, eloquent with deep drainage versus medium, eloquent, superficial); report the components.
The grade estimates surgical risk; it does not describe the natural history or haemorrhage risk.

limitations.text: Designed to estimate surgical risk; less applicable to radiosurgery or embolisation decisions.

limitations: Does not include age, rupture status, nidus diffuseness or perforator supply.
Size and eloquence assessment vary between raters.

confounders.effect: Can compress the nidus and change apparent size.
MRI and angiography may give different measurements.

guideSections.what: The sum of size (1–3), eloquence (0–1) and venous drainage (0–1), giving grades I–V.
guideSections.whenToUse: Describing brain AVMs and estimating surgical risk; communication between neurosurgery and neuroradiology.
guideSections.howToPerform: Measure the maximum nidus diameter on angiography or MRI. Decide whether adjacent brain is eloquent. Identify any deep venous drainage. Sum the points.
guideSections.clinicalContext: One input to multidisciplinary decisions, with the supplementary grade and the patient's presentation and preferences.

sources.citation: Spetzler RF, Martin NA. A proposed grading system for arteriovenous malformations. J Neurosurg. 1986;65(4):476-483.
